transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Your Name]. What brings you in today? How can I help you?

Hey. Uh... well, I guess I'm here because I haven't really had much of an appetite lately. For the last few weeks or so. 

Usually, after a shift, I'll grab something I like, but... lately it just sits there. I kind of just have to force down a few bites. So... yeah. That's mainly it.
Have you noticed any other changes, like losing weight, feeling more tired than usual, or feeling down?

I haven't really noticed the weight thing. But... yeah, I guess I've been feeling down. 

It's hard to explain, it's just... this heavy, flat feeling most days. Like, even when I'm home with my family, or just sitting in the break room on shift... I don't know. I'm just not really there. So... yeah.
Have you noticed a loss of interest or pleasure in activities that you usually enjoy, like hobbies or time with family?

Yeah... I guess so. Um. I used to do stuff. Like, go for morning runs, play some guitar... cook dinner. But lately I just keep skipping all that. It just... I don't know, it all feels like a chore. I just can't really get myself to care about doing any of it right now.
How long have you been feeling this way?
Um... I'd say about three weeks. Give or take. They, uh... they reorganized our security operations at the casino around then. Switched up my assignments. So... yeah. Since then, mostly.
Have you noticed that you're moving more slowly than usual, or have trouble sitting still?

Um... I guess so. The guys at work said something about it. 

Just... in briefings, they said I'm moving slower. Taking longer to answer when they ask me something. It's just... I don't know, it feels like my body and my mouth are just a step behind everyone else. So... yeah.
Have you found yourself feeling more guilty about things than usual, or like you're not worth much?
No, not really. I mean... I don't think so. Just... doing my job, I guess. Nothing to feel guilty about.
Have you found yourself thinking that life isn't worth living, or had any thoughts about harming yourself?

Um... no. I'm not planning to... hurt myself or anything like that. 

Just... I don't know. Sometimes I just think... maybe it wouldn't be the worst thing if I just didn't wake up. Just... so I wouldn't have to keep pushing through all this. But... yeah. I'm not gonna do anything.
Have you noticed a big drop in your energy lately, like feeling really tired even when you haven't done much?
Um... not really. I mean, I'm tired, but... I work long shifts. So, it's just normal tired, I guess. Nothing... nothing out of the ordinary.
Have you noticed a significant drop in your energy levels, even when you haven't been working long shifts?
Um... no, not really. Like I said, it's mostly just work. When I have time off, I just... I don't do much anyway. Just stay home. So I haven't really noticed anything like that.
Have you noticed any trouble focusing or thinking clearly lately, like during work or when trying to make decisions?

Um... maybe a little. Just... at work, mostly. 

When I'm watching the CCTV feeds, my mind kind of... drifts off. And then if I have to write up an incident report, I find myself having to read it over and over just to get through it. I guess... I don't know, I ended up making a couple mistakes lately that I normally wouldn't. But... yeah. That's about it.
Would you say that you’ve completely lost interest in all or almost all activities, even ones you used to enjoy a lot?

Um... I guess so. I don't know. 

I used to run in the mornings... play guitar sometimes. Cook. But... I haven't been doing any of that lately. I just skip it. It all just... feels like a chore now. I just don't really care to do it anymore.
Have you noticed that your movements or speech have been slowed down or, on the contrary, that you can't sit still and feel restless?

Um... not restless, no. But... I guess I've been a little slow. At least, some of the guys at work mentioned it. 

Just... during shift briefings and stuff, they said I'm moving slower. Taking longer to answer when they ask me something. I don't know... it just feels like my body and my mouth are kind of... a step behind everybody else. But I didn't really notice it until they said something.
Would you say your fatigue or low energy goes beyond what you would normally expect from your work schedule?
I don't think so. I mean... I work long shifts, sometimes nights. It's normal to be tired. I just... I'm just tired, that's all.
Would you say that absolutely nothing you do brings you any pleasure or satisfaction anymore?

Yeah, I guess. Like I said a minute ago... the running, playing guitar, cooking... none of it really does anything for me right now. It's just... I don't know, it all just feels like chores. I don't get any satisfaction out of it anymore.
Would you say that your mood has been consistently low every day for most of the day, even when things like work or your surroundings haven't changed?

Yeah, I suppose so. Most days, it's just... this heavy feeling. Flat, I guess. Even when nothing's really going wrong, like when I'm just sitting in the break room or... or at home with my family. I just... I don't feel like I'm really there. It's just kind of always there.

This duration is approaching but not yet meeting the full criteria for a major depressive episode (which requires at least two weeks of symptoms for diagnosis). However, the severity and persistence of symptoms support the retention of mild, moderate, and severe depressive episode codes (F32.0, F32.1, F32.2). Recurrent depressive disorder codes (F33.0, F33.1, F33.2) were ruled out due to insufficient evidence of prior episodes.

The patient reported a loss of interest in almost all activities, significant anhedonia, and psychomotor slowing. These symptoms support the presence of a moderate to severe depressive episode (F32.1 or F32.2). However, the absence of significant fatigue outside of work context and no clear presence of guilt, self-reproach, or marked worthlessness makes F32.0 less likely. Further clarification is needed regarding severity of symptoms to distinguish between F32.1 and F32.2.
